Fri

Aug 14Medium-low confidenceoutbound · 06:00–22:00 ET
METARMETAR — the routine surface observation issued hourly by the reporting station, with SPECI reports off-cycle, carrying ceiling, visibility, wind, temperature and altimeter. Issued by the observing station and distributed by aviationweather.gov. This is measured fact, not a forecast, and on this page it describes conditions right now, not this day. A current KLZU observation was read this run. It describes conditions now, not this trip day.TAFTAF — the Terminal Aerodrome Forecast, the highest-resolution aviation forecast available. The National Weather Service issues it four times a day, valid 24 to 30 hours, with explicit FM and TEMPO change groups. KLZU has no TAF station, so KPDK is used as a proxy. It is the strongest flight-category evidence this page can show. Beyond the TAF horizon of about 30 hours; no TAF exists at this range for any station.NWS-hrNWS hourly gridpoint forecast — the National Weather Service digital forecast for the grid cell containing KLZU, updated through the day and reaching about 156 hours. It gives hour-by-hour sky, wind and precipitation probability, and it is the spine of the change windows on this board. The NWS hourly gridpoint forecast reaches this day.NWS-dayNWS day/night outlook — the same National Weather Service grid summarised into day and night halves, reaching about 168 hours. Coarser than the hourly product but it covers one day further, so this page uses it only to describe spans the hourly forecast cannot reach. Not needed: this day is already covered by the finer-resolution hourly gridpoint forecast.MAVGFS MOS (MAV) — Model Output Statistics, the GFS model bias-corrected against decades of observations at this station. Issued by the National Weather Service four times a day in three-hourly steps out to about 72 hours. It carries an explicit ceiling and visibility category, so this page uses it to corroborate the flight category. Beyond the GFS MAV MOS horizon of about 72 hours, or no MAV row carried both a ceiling and a visibility for this day.MEXGFS extended MOS (MEX) — the extended-range MOS product, issued twice a day in twelve-hourly steps out to about 192 hours. Coarse, but the only station-calibrated numeric guidance that reaches the far end of a long weekend. This page shows it only as a flagged outlook and never promotes it into a short-range category. An extended GFS MEX outlook point describes part of this day. MEX publishes no ceiling or visibility, so it states no flight category; where its sky, precipitation, thunderstorm or obstruction fields are usable it is shown as a clearly labelled “(Predicted)” value.GFAGFA and prog charts — the Graphical Forecast for Aviation and the Weather Prediction Center surface progs, issued by the National Weather Service through the day; the surface prog series reaches 144 hours. They are raster images a pilot reads for fronts, pressure systems and precipitation shields. This page displays them with their issuing office and valid time and never interprets them: no category, wind, ceiling, ranking or go/no-go here is derived from an image. A published WPC surface chart matches this period and is shown in the dropdown with its issuing office and valid time. It is displayed, never interpreted.NOTAMFAA NOTAM (NMS) — Notices to Air Missions: closures, outages, obstacles and TFRs, issued continuously by the FAA and valid until cancelled. On this page they are advisory evidence about the airport, not weather, and they never change a flight category. NOTAMs were read for KLZU this run.

Coarser than the hourly product but it covers one day further, so this page uses it only to describe spans the hourly forecast cannot reach. The coarse NWS day/night outlook describes part of this day.MAVGFS MOS (MAV) — Model Output Statistics, the GFS model bias-corrected against decades of observations at this station. Issued by the National Weather Service four times a day in three-hourly steps out to about 72 hours. It carries an explicit ceiling and visibility category, so this page uses it to corroborate the flight category. Beyond the GFS MAV MOS horizon of about 72 hours, or no MAV row carried both a ceiling and a visibility for this day.MEXGFS extended MOS (MEX) — the extended-range MOS product, issued twice a day in twelve-hourly steps out to about 192 hours. Coarse, but the only station-calibrated numeric guidance that reaches the far end of a long weekend. This page shows it only as a flagged outlook and never promotes it into a short-range category. An extended GFS MEX outlook point describes part of this day. MEX publishes no ceiling or visibility, so it states no flight category; where its sky, precipitation, thunderstorm or obstruction fields are usable it is shown as a clearly labelled “(Predicted)” value.GFAGFA and prog charts — the Graphical Forecast for Aviation and the Weather Prediction Center surface progs, issued by the National Weather Service through the day; the surface prog series reaches 144 hours. They are raster images a pilot reads for fronts, pressure systems and precipitation shields. This page displays them with their issuing office and valid time and never interprets them: no category, wind, ceiling, ranking or go/no-go here is derived from an image. This period is past the 144-hour end of the published WPC surface prog series, so no chart covers it. That is the product's horizon, not a failure, and it says nothing about the weather.NOTAMFAA NOTAM (NMS) — Notices to Air Missions: closures, outages, obstacles and TFRs, issued continuously by the FAA and valid until cancelled. On this page they are advisory evidence about the airport, not weather, and they never change a flight category. NOTAMs were read for KLZU this run.

Short term

.. (This afternoon through Tuesday) Issued at 144 PM EDT Mon Aug 10 2026 Another round of isolated to scattered showers and thunderstorms expected again this afternoon and evening. The over all pattern has not changed much but the old boundary from yesterday is now oriented more E to W across North GA. Hi-Res models showing this front acting as a catalyst again today for storms to fire along. Main surface to mid level Bermuda ridge centered just off the GA/SC coast is strengthening and building west across FL and across the Gulf. This vertically stacked ridge axis stays south of the state keeping GA in westerly flow. This building ridge is not allowing the old boundary to move south and it may limit storm potential over central Georgia to more of an isolated chance. Currently expecting similar coverage as yesterday. With PWATs in the 1.8" to 2.1" range and MU CAPE values expected in the 1500-2300 J/kg range, the main threats will continue to be gusty winds, frequent lightning strikes, and locally heavy rainfall. An isolated severe storm or two can also be expected. Tuesday will be much of the same pattern although central Georgia could see a bit more coverage. Models showing a Wedge/Ridge building southwest down the eastern seaboard and pushing that old boundary into central GA. Temperature Tuesday will be a deg or two warmer than today especially across east central GA. We could see some locations have a couple of hours closer to 105 but should stay just below heat advisory criteria will have to keep a close eye on how things develop.

Long term

.. (Wednesday morning through next Sunday) Issued at 144 PM EDT Mon Aug 10 2026 The main story for the extended period will be rising temperatures and the potential for impactful heat late this week into the upcoming weekend. The set up responsible for these trends will be an eastward migrating mid-level ridge, currently over the Desert Southwest and high pressure at the surface. Temperatures are forecast to rise to the upper 80s to low 90s (outside of the higher elevations) by Wednesday, with temperatures trending upward a degree or two each day going forward. Increasing moisture will support the return of dewpoints in the mid-to-upper 70s and PWs in excess of 1.5". Thus, heat index values ('feels like' temperatures) return to triple digit values for most places heading into the next weekend. Heat headlines may be necessary in future forecasts. In the meantime, be mindful of the heat as you plan for any outdoor work or activities over the next 7 days. Any disturbances that translate through the the mid/upper level flow may act to locally enhance thunderstorm activity on any given day. A few MCSs (thunderstorm complexes) look to pass just to our north and east over the next few days but could clip parts of Northeast GA...something to watch as models generally struggle with the evolution of these features. Otherwise, expect at least low chances (20-30%) for afternoon and evening thunderstorms over the next 5-7 days.

KTRI OBS - VFR Bristol/Tri-Cities Arpt, TN, US · Tri-Cities TN/VAETE1h11Dist168 nm
METARMETAR — the routine surface observation issued hourly by the reporting station, with SPECI reports off-cycle, carrying ceiling, visibility, wind, temperature and altimeter. Issued by the observing station and distributed by aviationweather.gov. This is measured fact, not a forecast, and on this page it describes conditions right now, not this day. A current KTRI observation was read this run. It describes conditions now, not this trip day.TAFTAF — the Terminal Aerodrome Forecast, the highest-resolution aviation forecast available. The National Weather Service issues it four times a day, valid 24 to 30 hours, with explicit FM and TEMPO change groups. Airports without their own TAF station use a nearby proxy, which is a normal condition and not a fault. No usable TAF covers the planned dates at this airport (state: unavailable). A TAF reaches only about 30 hours, so a later trip day being uncovered is a horizon fact, not a fault.MAVGFS MOS (MAV) — Model Output Statistics, the GFS model bias-corrected against decades of observations at this station. Issued four times a day in three-hourly steps out to about 72 hours. It carries an explicit ceiling and visibility category, so this card uses it to resolve a day the TAF cannot reach. Beyond the 72 h GFS MOS horizon at this lead time. The product published normally; this day is simply past its reach, which is expected and is not a fault. Expected to be covered from about Tue Aug 11 · 12:00 AM ET. The extended GFS MOS (MEX) outlook does reach this day and is shown as a labelled rough outlook; it never states a flight category.MEXGFS extended MOS (MEX) — the extended-range MOS product, issued twice a day in twelve-hourly steps out to about 192 hours. Coarse, but the only station-calibrated numeric guidance that reaches the far end of a long weekend. This card shows it only as a labelled rough outlook and never as a resolved forecast. A station-calibrated MEX MOS product was read for this airport this run (state: ok).GFAGFA and prog charts — the Graphical Forecast for Aviation and the Weather Prediction Center surface progs, issued by the National Weather Service through the day; the surface prog series reaches 144 hours. They are raster images a pilot reads for fronts, pressure systems and precipitation shields. This page displays them with their issuing office and valid time and never interprets them: no category, wind, ceiling, ranking or go/no-go here is derived from an image. A published WPC surface chart matches this period and is shown in the dropdown with its issuing office and valid time. It is displayed, never interpreted.NOTAMFAA NOTAM (NMS) — Notices to Air Missions: closures, outages, obstacles and TFRs, issued continuously by the FAA and valid until cancelled. On this page they are advisory evidence about the airport, not weather, and they never change a flight category. NOTAMs were read for KTRI this run.

METARMETAR — the routine surface observation issued hourly by the reporting station, with SPECI reports off-cycle, carrying ceiling, visibility, wind, temperature and altimeter. Issued by the observing station and distributed by aviationweather.gov. This is measured fact, not a forecast, and on this page it describes conditions right now, not this day. A current KROA observation was read this run. It describes conditions now, not this trip day.TAFTAF — the Terminal Aerodrome Forecast, the highest-resolution aviation forecast available. The National Weather Service issues it four times a day, valid 24 to 30 hours, with explicit FM and TEMPO change groups. Airports without their own TAF station use a nearby proxy, which is a normal condition and not a fault. No usable TAF covers the planned dates at this airport (state: unavailable). A TAF reaches only about 30 hours, so a later trip day being uncovered is a horizon fact, not a fault.MAVGFS MOS (MAV) — Model Output Statistics, the GFS model bias-corrected against decades of observations at this station. Issued four times a day in three-hourly steps out to about 72 hours. It carries an explicit ceiling and visibility category, so this card uses it to resolve a day the TAF cannot reach. Beyond the 72 h GFS MOS horizon at this lead time. The product published normally; this day is simply past its reach, which is expected and is not a fault. Expected to be covered from about Tue Aug 11 · 12:00 AM ET. The extended GFS MOS (MEX) outlook does reach this day and is shown as a labelled rough outlook; it never states a flight category.MEXGFS extended MOS (MEX) — the extended-range MOS product, issued twice a day in twelve-hourly steps out to about 192 hours. Coarse, but the only station-calibrated numeric guidance that reaches the far end of a long weekend. This card shows it only as a labelled rough outlook and never as a resolved forecast. A station-calibrated MEX MOS product was read for this airport this run (state: ok).GFAGFA and prog charts — the Graphical Forecast for Aviation and the Weather Prediction Center surface progs, issued by the National Weather Service through the day; the surface prog series reaches 144 hours. They are raster images a pilot reads for fronts, pressure systems and precipitation shields. This page displays them with their issuing office and valid time and never interprets them: no category, wind, ceiling, ranking or go/no-go here is derived from an image. A published WPC surface chart matches this period and is shown in the dropdown with its issuing office and valid time. It is displayed, never interpreted.NOTAMFAA NOTAM (NMS) — Notices to Air Missions: closures, outages, obstacles and TFRs, issued continuously by the FAA and valid until cancelled. KSHD OBS - VFR Staunton/Shenandoah Valley Rgnl, VA, US · Shenandoah valleyETE2h25Dist355 nm
METARMETAR — the routine surface observation issued hourly by the reporting station, with SPECI reports off-cycle, carrying ceiling, visibility, wind, temperature and altimeter. Issued by the observing station and distributed by aviationweather.gov. This is measured fact, not a forecast, and on this page it describes conditions right now, not this day. A current KSHD observation was read this run. It describes conditions now, not this trip day.TAFTAF — the Terminal Aerodrome Forecast, the highest-resolution aviation forecast available. The National Weather Service issues it four times a day, valid 24 to 30 hours, with explicit FM and TEMPO change groups. Airports without their own TAF station use a nearby proxy, which is a normal condition and not a fault. No usable TAF covers the planned dates at this airport (state: unavailable). A TAF reaches only about 30 hours, so a later trip day being uncovered is a horizon fact, not a fault. This airport has no TAF station of its own, so KCHO is used as a proxy; that is a normal condition, not a failure.MAVGFS MOS (MAV) — Model Output Statistics, the GFS model bias-corrected against decades of observations at this station. Issued four times a day in three-hourly steps out to about 72 hours. It carries an explicit ceiling and visibility category, so this card uses it to resolve a day the TAF cannot reach. Beyond the 72 h GFS MOS horizon at this lead time. The product published normally; this day is simply past its reach, which is expected and is not a fault. Expected to be covered from about Tue Aug 11 · 12:00 AM ET. The extended GFS MOS (MEX) outlook does reach this day and is shown as a labelled rough outlook; it never states a flight category.MEXGFS extended MOS (MEX) — the extended-range MOS product, issued twice a day in twelve-hourly steps out to about 192 hours. Coarse, but the only station-calibrated numeric guidance that reaches the far end of a long weekend. This card shows it only as a labelled rough outlook and never as a resolved forecast. A station-calibrated MEX MOS product was read for this airport this run (state: ok).GFAGFA and prog charts — the Graphical Forecast for Aviation and the Weather Prediction Center surface progs, issued by the National Weather Service through the day; the surface prog series reaches 144 hours. They are raster images a pilot reads for fronts, pressure systems and precipitation shields. This page displays them with their issuing office and valid time and never interprets them: no category, wind, ceiling, ranking or go/no-go here is derived from an image. A published WPC surface chart matches this period and is shown in the dropdown with its issuing office and valid time. It is displayed, never interpreted.NOTAMFAA NOTAM (NMS) — Notices to Air Missions: closures, outages, obstacles and TFRs, issued continuously by the FAA and valid until cancelled. On this page they are advisory evidence about the airport, not weather, and they never change a flight category. NOTAMs were read for KSHD this run.

Issued by the observing station and distributed by aviationweather.gov. This is measured fact, not a forecast, and on this page it describes conditions right now, not this day. A current KSAV observation was read this run. It describes conditions now, not this trip day.TAFTAF — the Terminal Aerodrome Forecast, the highest-resolution aviation forecast available. The National Weather Service issues it four times a day, valid 24 to 30 hours, with explicit FM and TEMPO change groups. Airports without their own TAF station use a nearby proxy, which is a normal condition and not a fault. No usable TAF covers the planned dates at this airport (state: unavailable). A TAF reaches only about 30 hours, so a later trip day being uncovered is a horizon fact, not a fault.MAVGFS MOS (MAV) — Model Output Statistics, the GFS model bias-corrected against decades of observations at this station. Issued four times a day in three-hourly steps out to about 72 hours. It carries an explicit ceiling and visibility category, so this card uses it to resolve a day the TAF cannot reach. Beyond the 72 h GFS MOS horizon at this lead time. The product published normally; this day is simply past its reach, which is expected and is not a fault. Expected to be covered from about Tue Aug 11 · 12:00 AM ET. The extended GFS MOS (MEX) outlook does reach this day and is shown as a labelled rough outlook; it never states a flight category.MEXGFS extended MOS (MEX) — the extended-range MOS product, issued twice a day in twelve-hourly steps out to about 192 hours. Coarse, but the only station-calibrated numeric guidance that reaches the far end of a long weekend. This card shows it only as a labelled rough outlook and never as a resolved forecast. A station-calibrated MEX MOS product was read for this airport this run (state: ok).GFAGFA and prog charts — the Graphical Forecast for Aviation and the Weather Prediction Center surface progs, issued by the National Weather Service through the day; the surface prog series reaches 144 hours. They are raster images a pilot reads for fronts, pressure systems and precipitation shields. This page displays them with their issuing office and valid time and never interprets them: no category, wind, ceiling, ranking or go/no-go here is derived from an image. A published WPC surface chart matches this period and is shown in the dropdown with its issuing office and valid time. It is displayed, never interpreted.NOTAMFAA NOTAM (NMS) — Notices to Air Missions: closures, outages, obstacles and TFRs, issued continuously by the FAA and valid until cancelled. On this page they are advisory evidence about the airport, not weather, and they never change a flight category. NOTAMs were read for KSAV this run.

KJZI OBS - VFR Charleston Exec, SC, US · Charleston ExecETE1h28Dist213 nm
METARMETAR — the routine surface observation issued hourly by the reporting station, with SPECI reports off-cycle, carrying ceiling, visibility, wind, temperature and altimeter. Issued by the observing station and distributed by aviationweather.gov. This is measured fact, not a forecast, and on this page it describes conditions right now, not this day. A current KJZI observation was read this run. It describes conditions now, not this trip day.TAFTAF — the Terminal Aerodrome Forecast, the highest-resolution aviation forecast available. The National Weather Service issues it four times a day, valid 24 to 30 hours, with explicit FM and TEMPO change groups. Airports without their own TAF station use a nearby proxy, which is a normal condition and not a fault. No usable TAF covers the planned dates at this airport (state: unavailable). A TAF reaches only about 30 hours, so a later trip day being uncovered is a horizon fact, not a fault.MAVGFS MOS (MAV) — Model Output Statistics, the GFS model bias-corrected against decades of observations at this station. Issued four times a day in three-hourly steps out to about 72 hours. It carries an explicit ceiling and visibility category, so this card uses it to resolve a day the TAF cannot reach. Beyond the 72 h GFS MOS horizon at this lead time. The product published normally; this day is simply past its reach, which is expected and is not a fault. Expected to be covered from about Tue Aug 11 · 12:00 AM ET. The extended GFS MOS (MEX) outlook does reach this day and is shown as a labelled rough outlook; it never states a flight category.MEXGFS extended MOS (MEX) — the extended-range MOS product, issued twice a day in twelve-hourly steps out to about 192 hours. Coarse, but the only station-calibrated numeric guidance that reaches the far end of a long weekend. This card shows it only as a labelled rough outlook and never as a resolved forecast. A station-calibrated MEX MOS product was read for this airport this run (state: ok).GFAGFA and prog charts — the Graphical Forecast for Aviation and the Weather Prediction Center surface progs, issued by the National Weather Service through the day; the surface prog series reaches 144 hours. They are raster images a pilot reads for fronts, pressure systems and precipitation shields. This page displays them with their issuing office and valid time and never interprets them: no category, wind, ceiling, ranking or go/no-go here is derived from an image. A published WPC surface chart matches this period and is shown in the dropdown with its issuing office and valid time. It is displayed, never interpreted.NOTAMFAA NOTAM (NMS) — Notices to Air Missions: closures, outages, obstacles and TFRs, issued continuously by the FAA and valid until cancelled. On this page they are advisory evidence about the airport, not weather, and they never change a flight category. NOTAMs were read for KJZI this run.

KSGJ OBS - VFR St Augustine Arpt, FL, US · St Augustine FLETE1h55Dist276 nm
METARMETAR — the routine surface observation issued hourly by the reporting station, with SPECI reports off-cycle, carrying ceiling, visibility, wind, temperature and altimeter. Issued by the observing station and distributed by aviationweather.gov. This is measured fact, not a forecast, and on this page it describes conditions right now, not this day. A current KSGJ observation was read this run. It describes conditions now, not this trip day.TAFTAF — the Terminal Aerodrome Forecast, the highest-resolution aviation forecast available. The National Weather Service issues it four times a day, valid 24 to 30 hours, with explicit FM and TEMPO change groups. Airports without their own TAF station use a nearby proxy, which is a normal condition and not a fault. No usable TAF covers the planned dates at this airport (state: unavailable). A TAF reaches only about 30 hours, so a later trip day being uncovered is a horizon fact, not a fault.MAVGFS MOS (MAV) — Model Output Statistics, the GFS model bias-corrected against decades of observations at this station. Issued four times a day in three-hourly steps out to about 72 hours. It carries an explicit ceiling and visibility category, so this card uses it to resolve a day the TAF cannot reach. Beyond the 72 h GFS MOS horizon at this lead time. The product published normally; this day is simply past its reach, which is expected and is not a fault. Expected to be covered from about Tue Aug 11 · 12:00 AM ET. The extended GFS MOS (MEX) outlook does reach this day and is shown as a labelled rough outlook; it never states a flight category.MEXGFS extended MOS (MEX) — the extended-range MOS product, issued twice a day in twelve-hourly steps out to about 192 hours. Coarse, but the only station-calibrated numeric guidance that reaches the far end of a long weekend. This card shows it only as a labelled rough outlook and never as a resolved forecast. A station-calibrated MEX MOS product was read for this airport this run (state: ok).GFAGFA and prog charts — the Graphical Forecast for Aviation and the Weather Prediction Center surface progs, issued by the National Weather Service through the day; the surface prog series reaches 144 hours. They are raster images a pilot reads for fronts, pressure systems and precipitation shields. This page displays them with their issuing office and valid time and never interprets them: no category, wind, ceiling, ranking or go/no-go here is derived from an image. A published WPC surface chart matches this period and is shown in the dropdown with its issuing office and valid time. It is displayed, never interpreted.NOTAMFAA NOTAM (NMS) — Notices to Air Missions: closures, outages, obstacles and TFRs, issued continuously by the FAA and valid until cancelled. On this page they are advisory evidence about the airport, not weather, and they never change a flight category. NOTAMs were read for KSGJ this run.

The National Weather Service issues it four times a day, valid 24 to 30 hours, with explicit FM and TEMPO change groups. Airports without their own TAF station use a nearby proxy, which is a normal condition and not a fault. No usable TAF covers the planned dates at this airport (state: unavailable). A TAF reaches only about 30 hours, so a later trip day being uncovered is a horizon fact, not a fault. This airport has no TAF station of its own, so KDAB is used as a proxy; that is a normal condition, not a failure.MAVGFS MOS (MAV) — Model Output Statistics, the GFS model bias-corrected against decades of observations at this station. Issued four times a day in three-hourly steps out to about 72 hours. It carries an explicit ceiling and visibility category, so this card uses it to resolve a day the TAF cannot reach. Beyond the 72 h GFS MOS horizon at this lead time. The product published normally; this day is simply past its reach, which is expected and is not a fault. KCRE OBS - VFR North Myrtle Beach/Grand Strand Arpt, SC, US · N Myrtle BeachETE1h49Dist261 nm
METARMETAR — the routine surface observation issued hourly by the reporting station, with SPECI reports off-cycle, carrying ceiling, visibility, wind, temperature and altimeter. Issued by the observing station and distributed by aviationweather.gov. This is measured fact, not a forecast, and on this page it describes conditions right now, not this day. A current KCRE observation was read this run. It describes conditions now, not this trip day.TAFTAF — the Terminal Aerodrome Forecast, the highest-resolution aviation forecast available. The National Weather Service issues it four times a day, valid 24 to 30 hours, with explicit FM and TEMPO change groups. Airports without their own TAF station use a nearby proxy, which is a normal condition and not a fault. No usable TAF covers the planned dates at this airport (state: unavailable). A TAF reaches only about 30 hours, so a later trip day being uncovered is a horizon fact, not a fault. This airport has no TAF station of its own, so KMYR is used as a proxy; that is a normal condition, not a failure.MAVGFS MOS (MAV) — Model Output Statistics, the GFS model bias-corrected against decades of observations at this station. Issued four times a day in three-hourly steps out to about 72 hours. It carries an explicit ceiling and visibility category, so this card uses it to resolve a day the TAF cannot reach. Beyond the 72 h GFS MOS horizon at this lead time. The product published normally; this day is simply past its reach, which is expected and is not a fault. Expected to be covered from about Tue Aug 11 · 12:00 AM ET. The extended GFS MOS (MEX) outlook does reach this day and is shown as a labelled rough outlook; it never states a flight category.MEXGFS extended MOS (MEX) — the extended-range MOS product, issued twice a day in twelve-hourly steps out to about 192 hours. Coarse, but the only station-calibrated numeric guidance that reaches the far end of a long weekend. This card shows it only as a labelled rough outlook and never as a resolved forecast. A station-calibrated MEX MOS product was read for this airport this run (state: ok).GFAGFA and prog charts — the Graphical Forecast for Aviation and the Weather Prediction Center surface progs, issued by the National Weather Service through the day; the surface prog series reaches 144 hours. They are raster images a pilot reads for fronts, pressure systems and precipitation shields. This page displays them with their issuing office and valid time and never interprets them: no category, wind, ceiling, ranking or go/no-go here is derived from an image. A published WPC surface chart matches this period and is shown in the dropdown with its issuing office and valid time. It is displayed, never interpreted.NOTAMFAA NOTAM (NMS) — Notices to Air Missions: closures, outages, obstacles and TFRs, issued continuously by the FAA and valid until cancelled. On this page they are advisory evidence about the airport, not weather, and they never change a flight category. NOTAMs were read for KCRE this run.

KPNS OBS - VFR Pensacola Intl, FL, US · Pensacola (Class C)ETE1h51Dist267 nm
METARMETAR — the routine surface observation issued hourly by the reporting station, with SPECI reports off-cycle, carrying ceiling, visibility, wind, temperature and altimeter. Issued by the observing station and distributed by aviationweather.gov. This is measured fact, not a forecast, and on this page it describes conditions right now, not this day. A current KPNS observation was read this run. It describes conditions now, not this trip day.TAFTAF — the Terminal Aerodrome Forecast, the highest-resolution aviation forecast available. The National Weather Service issues it four times a day, valid 24 to 30 hours, with explicit FM and TEMPO change groups. Airports without their own TAF station use a nearby proxy, which is a normal condition and not a fault. No usable TAF covers the planned dates at this airport (state: unavailable). A TAF reaches only about 30 hours, so a later trip day being uncovered is a horizon fact, not a fault.MAVGFS MOS (MAV) — Model Output Statistics, the GFS model bias-corrected against decades of observations at this station. Issued four times a day in three-hourly steps out to about 72 hours. It carries an explicit ceiling and visibility category, so this card uses it to resolve a day the TAF cannot reach. Beyond the 72 h GFS MOS horizon at this lead time. The product published normally; this day is simply past its reach, which is expected and is not a fault. Expected to be covered from about Tue Aug 11 · 12:00 AM ET. The extended GFS MOS (MEX) outlook does reach this day and is shown as a labelled rough outlook; it never states a flight category.MEXGFS extended MOS (MEX) — the extended-range MOS product, issued twice a day in twelve-hourly steps out to about 192 hours. Coarse, but the only station-calibrated numeric guidance that reaches the far end of a long weekend. This card shows it only as a labelled rough outlook and never as a resolved forecast. A station-calibrated MEX MOS product was read for this airport this run (state: ok).GFAGFA and prog charts — the Graphical Forecast for Aviation and the Weather Prediction Center surface progs, issued by the National Weather Service through the day; the surface prog series reaches 144 hours. They are raster images a pilot reads for fronts, pressure systems and precipitation shields. This page displays them with their issuing office and valid time and never interprets them: no category, wind, ceiling, ranking or go/no-go here is derived from an image. A published WPC surface chart matches this period and is shown in the dropdown with its issuing office and valid time. It is displayed, never interpreted.NOTAMFAA NOTAM (NMS) — Notices to Air Missions: closures, outages, obstacles and TFRs, issued continuously by the FAA and valid until cancelled. On this page they are advisory evidence about the airport, not weather, and they never change a flight category. NOTAMs were read for KPNS this run.

KDAB OBS - VFR Daytona Beach Intl, FL, US · Daytona Beach (Class C)ETE2h13Dist324 nm
METARMETAR — the routine surface observation issued hourly by the reporting station, with SPECI reports off-cycle, carrying ceiling, visibility, wind, temperature and altimeter. Issued by the observing station and distributed by aviationweather.gov. This is measured fact, not a forecast, and on this page it describes conditions right now, not this day. A current KDAB observation was read this run. It describes conditions now, not this trip day.TAFTAF — the Terminal Aerodrome Forecast, the highest-resolution aviation forecast available. The National Weather Service issues it four times a day, valid 24 to 30 hours, with explicit FM and TEMPO change groups. Airports without their own TAF station use a nearby proxy, which is a normal condition and not a fault. No usable TAF covers the planned dates at this airport (state: unavailable). A TAF reaches only about 30 hours, so a later trip day being uncovered is a horizon fact, not a fault.MAVGFS MOS (MAV) — Model Output Statistics, the GFS model bias-corrected against decades of observations at this station. Issued four times a day in three-hourly steps out to about 72 hours. It carries an explicit ceiling and visibility category, so this card uses it to resolve a day the TAF cannot reach. Beyond the 72 h GFS MOS horizon at this lead time. The product published normally; this day is simply past its reach, which is expected and is not a fault. Expected to be covered from about Tue Aug 11 · 12:00 AM ET. The extended GFS MOS (MEX) outlook does reach this day and is shown as a labelled rough outlook; it never states a flight category.MEXGFS extended MOS (MEX) — the extended-range MOS product, issued twice a day in twelve-hourly steps out to about 192 hours. Coarse, but the only station-calibrated numeric guidance that reaches the far end of a long weekend. This card shows it only as a labelled rough outlook and never as a resolved forecast. A station-calibrated MEX MOS product was read for this airport this run (state: ok).GFAGFA and prog charts — the Graphical Forecast for Aviation and the Weather Prediction Center surface progs, issued by the National Weather Service through the day; the surface prog series reaches 144 hours. They are raster images a pilot reads for fronts, pressure systems and precipitation shields. This page displays them with their issuing office and valid time and never interprets them: no category, wind, ceiling, ranking or go/no-go here is derived from an image. A published WPC surface chart matches this period and is shown in the dropdown with its issuing office and valid time. It is displayed, never interpreted.NOTAMFAA NOTAM (NMS) — Notices to Air Missions: closures, outages, obstacles and TFRs, issued continuously by the FAA and valid until cancelled. On this page they are advisory evidence about the airport, not weather, and they never change a flight category. NOTAMs were read for KDAB this run.

KSRQ OBS - VFR Sarasota-Bradenton Intl, FL, US · Sarasota-BradentonETE2h43Dist402 nm
METARMETAR — the routine surface observation issued hourly by the reporting station, with SPECI reports off-cycle, carrying ceiling, visibility, wind, temperature and altimeter. Issued by the observing station and distributed by aviationweather.gov. This is measured fact, not a forecast, and on this page it describes conditions right now, not this day. A current KSRQ observation was read this run. It describes conditions now, not this trip day.TAFTAF — the Terminal Aerodrome Forecast, the highest-resolution aviation forecast available. The National Weather Service issues it four times a day, valid 24 to 30 hours, with explicit FM and TEMPO change groups. Airports without their own TAF station use a nearby proxy, which is a normal condition and not a fault. No usable TAF covers the planned dates at this airport (state: unavailable). A TAF reaches only about 30 hours, so a later trip day being uncovered is a horizon fact, not a fault.MAVGFS MOS (MAV) — Model Output Statistics, the GFS model bias-corrected against decades of observations at this station. Issued four times a day in three-hourly steps out to about 72 hours. It carries an explicit ceiling and visibility category, so this card uses it to resolve a day the TAF cannot reach. Beyond the 72 h GFS MOS horizon at this lead time. The product published normally; this day is simply past its reach, which is expected and is not a fault. Expected to be covered from about Tue Aug 11 · 12:00 AM ET. The extended GFS MOS (MEX) outlook does reach this day and is shown as a labelled rough outlook; it never states a flight category.MEXGFS extended MOS (MEX) — the extended-range MOS product, issued twice a day in twelve-hourly steps out to about 192 hours. Coarse, but the only station-calibrated numeric guidance that reaches the far end of a long weekend. This card shows it only as a labelled rough outlook and never as a resolved forecast. A station-calibrated MEX MOS product was read for this airport this run (state: ok).GFAGFA and prog charts — the Graphical Forecast for Aviation and the Weather Prediction Center surface progs, issued by the National Weather Service through the day; the surface prog series reaches 144 hours. They are raster images a pilot reads for fronts, pressure systems and precipitation shields. This page displays them with their issuing office and valid time and never interprets them: no category, wind, ceiling, ranking or go/no-go here is derived from an image. A published WPC surface chart matches this period and is shown in the dropdown with its issuing office and valid time. It is displayed, never interpreted.NOTAMFAA NOTAM (NMS) — Notices to Air Missions: closures, outages, obstacles and TFRs, issued continuously by the FAA and valid until cancelled. On this page they are advisory evidence about the airport, not weather, and they never change a flight category. NOTAMs were read for KSRQ this run.

KJKA OBS - VFR Gulf Shores/Edwards Arpt, AL, US · Gulf Shores ALETE2h01Dist291 nm
METARMETAR — the routine surface observation issued hourly by the reporting station, with SPECI reports off-cycle, carrying ceiling, visibility, wind, temperature and altimeter. Issued by the observing station and distributed by aviationweather.gov. This is measured fact, not a forecast, and on this page it describes conditions right now, not this day. A current KJKA observation was read this run. It describes conditions now, not this trip day.TAFTAF — the Terminal Aerodrome Forecast, the highest-resolution aviation forecast available. The National Weather Service issues it four times a day, valid 24 to 30 hours, with explicit FM and TEMPO change groups. Airports without their own TAF station use a nearby proxy, which is a normal condition and not a fault. No usable TAF covers the planned dates at this airport (state: unavailable). A TAF reaches only about 30 hours, so a later trip day being uncovered is a horizon fact, not a fault.MAVGFS MOS (MAV) — Model Output Statistics, the GFS model bias-corrected against decades of observations at this station. Issued four times a day in three-hourly steps out to about 72 hours. It carries an explicit ceiling and visibility category, so this card uses it to resolve a day the TAF cannot reach. Beyond the 72 h GFS MOS horizon at this lead time. The product published normally; this day is simply past its reach, which is expected and is not a fault. Expected to be covered from about Tue Aug 11 · 12:00 AM ET. The extended GFS MOS (MEX) outlook does reach this day and is shown as a labelled rough outlook; it never states a flight category.MEXGFS extended MOS (MEX) — the extended-range MOS product, issued twice a day in twelve-hourly steps out to about 192 hours. Coarse, but the only station-calibrated numeric guidance that reaches the far end of a long weekend. This card shows it only as a labelled rough outlook and never as a resolved forecast. A station-calibrated MEX MOS product was read for this airport this run (state: ok).GFAGFA and prog charts — the Graphical Forecast for Aviation and the Weather Prediction Center surface progs, issued by the National Weather Service through the day; the surface prog series reaches 144 hours. They are raster images a pilot reads for fronts, pressure systems and precipitation shields. This page displays them with their issuing office and valid time and never interprets them: no category, wind, ceiling, ranking or go/no-go here is derived from an image. A published WPC surface chart matches this period and is shown in the dropdown with its issuing office and valid time. It is displayed, never interpreted.NOTAMFAA NOTAM (NMS) — Notices to Air Missions: closures, outages, obstacles and TFRs, issued continuously by the FAA and valid until cancelled. On this page they are advisory evidence about the airport, not weather, and they never change a flight category. NOTAMs were read for KJKA this run.

METARMETAR — the routine surface observation issued hourly by the reporting station, with SPECI reports off-cycle, carrying ceiling, visibility, wind, temperature and altimeter. Issued by the observing station and distributed by aviationweather.gov. This is measured fact, not a forecast, and on this page it describes conditions right now, not this day. A current KHSA observation was read this run. It describes conditions now, not this trip day.TAFTAF — the Terminal Aerodrome Forecast, the highest-resolution aviation forecast available. The National Weather Service issues it four times a day, valid 24 to 30 hours, with explicit FM and TEMPO change groups. Airports without their own TAF station use a nearby proxy, which is a normal condition and not a fault. No usable TAF covers the planned dates at this airport (state: unavailable). A TAF reaches only about 30 hours, so a later trip day being uncovered is a horizon fact, not a fault. This airport has no TAF station of its own, so KGPT is used as a proxy; that is a normal condition, not a failure.MAVGFS MOS (MAV) — Model Output Statistics, the GFS model bias-corrected against decades of observations at this station. Issued four times a day in three-hourly steps out to about 72 hours. It carries an explicit ceiling and visibility category, so this card uses it to resolve a day the TAF cannot reach. Beyond the 72 h GFS MOS horizon at this lead time. The product published normally; this day is simply past its reach, which is expected and is not a fault. Expected to be covered from about Tue Aug 11 · 12:00 AM ET. The extended GFS MOS (MEX) outlook does reach this day and is shown as a labelled rough outlook; it never states a flight category.MEXGFS extended MOS (MEX) — the extended-range MOS product, issued twice a day in twelve-hourly steps out to about 192 hours. Coarse, but the only station-calibrated numeric guidance that reaches the far end of a long weekend. This card shows it only as a labelled rough outlook and never as a resolved forecast. A station-calibrated MEX MOS product was read for this airport this run (state: ok).GFAGFA and prog charts — the Graphical Forecast for Aviation and the Weather Prediction Center surface progs, issued by the National Weather Service through the day; the surface prog series reaches 144 hours. They are raster images a pilot reads for fronts, pressure systems and precipitation shields. This page displays them with their issuing office and valid time and never interprets them: no category, wind, ceiling, ranking or go/no-go here is derived from an image. A published WPC surface chart matches this period and is shown in the dropdown with its issuing office and valid time. It is displayed, never interpreted.NOTAMFAA NOTAM (NMS) — Notices to Air Missions: closures, outages, obstacles and TFRs, issued continuously by the FAA and valid until cancelled. On this page they are advisory evidence about the airport, not weather, and they never change a flight category. NOTAMs were read for KHSA this run.

KOPF OBS - VFR Miami/Opa Locka Arpt, FL, US · Miami-Opa LockaETE3h30Dist521 nm
METARMETAR — the routine surface observation issued hourly by the reporting station, with SPECI reports off-cycle, carrying ceiling, visibility, wind, temperature and altimeter. Issued by the observing station and distributed by aviationweather.gov. This is measured fact, not a forecast, and on this page it describes conditions right now, not this day. A current KOPF observation was read this run. It describes conditions now, not this trip day.TAFTAF — the Terminal Aerodrome Forecast, the highest-resolution aviation forecast available. The National Weather Service issues it four times a day, valid 24 to 30 hours, with explicit FM and TEMPO change groups. Airports without their own TAF station use a nearby proxy, which is a normal condition and not a fault. No usable TAF covers the planned dates at this airport (state: unavailable). A TAF reaches only about 30 hours, so a later trip day being uncovered is a horizon fact, not a fault.MAVGFS MOS (MAV) — Model Output Statistics, the GFS model bias-corrected against decades of observations at this station. Issued four times a day in three-hourly steps out to about 72 hours. It carries an explicit ceiling and visibility category, so this card uses it to resolve a day the TAF cannot reach. Beyond the 72 h GFS MOS horizon at this lead time. The product published normally; this day is simply past its reach, which is expected and is not a fault. Expected to be covered from about Tue Aug 11 · 12:00 AM ET. The extended GFS MOS (MEX) outlook does reach this day and is shown as a labelled rough outlook; it never states a flight category.MEXGFS extended MOS (MEX) — the extended-range MOS product, issued twice a day in twelve-hourly steps out to about 192 hours. Coarse, but the only station-calibrated numeric guidance that reaches the far end of a long weekend. This card shows it only as a labelled rough outlook and never as a resolved forecast. A station-calibrated MEX MOS product was read for this airport this run (state: ok).GFAGFA and prog charts — the Graphical Forecast for Aviation and the Weather Prediction Center surface progs, issued by the National Weather Service through the day; the surface prog series reaches 144 hours. They are raster images a pilot reads for fronts, pressure systems and precipitation shields. This page displays them with their issuing office and valid time and never interprets them: no category, wind, ceiling, ranking or go/no-go here is derived from an image. A published WPC surface chart matches this period and is shown in the dropdown with its issuing office and valid time. It is displayed, never interpreted.NOTAMFAA NOTAM (NMS) — Notices to Air Missions: closures, outages, obstacles and TFRs, issued continuously by the FAA and valid until cancelled. On this page they are advisory evidence about the airport, not weather, and they never change a flight category. NOTAMs were read for KOPF this run.

KHPN OBS - IFR White Plains/Westchester Cnty, NY, US · White Plains NYETE4h18Dist647 nm
METARMETAR — the routine surface observation issued hourly by the reporting station, with SPECI reports off-cycle, carrying ceiling, visibility, wind, temperature and altimeter. Issued by the observing station and distributed by aviationweather.gov. This is measured fact, not a forecast, and on this page it describes conditions right now, not this day. A current KHPN observation was read this run. It describes conditions now, not this trip day.TAFTAF — the Terminal Aerodrome Forecast, the highest-resolution aviation forecast available. The National Weather Service issues it four times a day, valid 24 to 30 hours, with explicit FM and TEMPO change groups. Airports without their own TAF station use a nearby proxy, which is a normal condition and not a fault. No usable TAF covers the planned dates at this airport (state: unavailable). A TAF reaches only about 30 hours, so a later trip day being uncovered is a horizon fact, not a fault.MAVGFS MOS (MAV) — Model Output Statistics, the GFS model bias-corrected against decades of observations at this station. Issued four times a day in three-hourly steps out to about 72 hours. It carries an explicit ceiling and visibility category, so this card uses it to resolve a day the TAF cannot reach. Beyond the 72 h GFS MOS horizon at this lead time. The product published normally; this day is simply past its reach, which is expected and is not a fault. Expected to be covered from about Tue Aug 11 · 12:00 AM ET. The extended GFS MOS (MEX) outlook does reach this day and is shown as a labelled rough outlook; it never states a flight category.MEXGFS extended MOS (MEX) — the extended-range MOS product, issued twice a day in twelve-hourly steps out to about 192 hours. Coarse, but the only station-calibrated numeric guidance that reaches the far end of a long weekend. This card shows it only as a labelled rough outlook and never as a resolved forecast. A station-calibrated MEX MOS product was read for this airport this run (state: ok).GFAGFA and prog charts — the Graphical Forecast for Aviation and the Weather Prediction Center surface progs, issued by the National Weather Service through the day; the surface prog series reaches 144 hours. They are raster images a pilot reads for fronts, pressure systems and precipitation shields. This page displays them with their issuing office and valid time and never interprets them: no category, wind, ceiling, ranking or go/no-go here is derived from an image. A published WPC surface chart matches this period and is shown in the dropdown with its issuing office and valid time. It is displayed, never interpreted.NOTAMFAA NOTAM (NMS) — Notices to Air Missions: closures, outages, obstacles and TFRs, issued continuously by the FAA and valid until cancelled. On this page they are advisory evidence about the airport, not weather, and they never change a flight category. NOTAMs were read for KHPN this run.

METARMETAR — the routine surface observation issued hourly by the reporting station, with SPECI reports off-cycle, carrying ceiling, visibility, wind, temperature and altimeter. Issued by the observing station and distributed by aviationweather.gov. This is measured fact, not a forecast, and on this page it describes conditions right now, not this day. A current KBED observation was read this run. It describes conditions now, not this trip day.TAFTAF — the Terminal Aerodrome Forecast, the highest-resolution aviation forecast available. The National Weather Service issues it four times a day, valid 24 to 30 hours, with explicit FM and TEMPO change groups. Airports without their own TAF station use a nearby proxy, which is a normal condition and not a fault. No usable TAF covers the planned dates at this airport (state: unavailable). A TAF reaches only about 30 hours, so a later trip day being uncovered is a horizon fact, not a fault.MAVGFS MOS (MAV) — Model Output Statistics, the GFS model bias-corrected against decades of observations at this station. Issued four times a day in three-hourly steps out to about 72 hours. It carries an explicit ceiling and visibility category, so this card uses it to resolve a day the TAF cannot reach. Beyond the 72 h GFS MOS horizon at this lead time. The product published normally; this day is simply past its reach, which is expected and is not a fault. Expected to be covered from about Tue Aug 11 · 12:00 AM ET. The extended GFS MOS (MEX) outlook does reach this day and is shown as a labelled rough outlook; it never states a flight category.MEXGFS extended MOS (MEX) — the extended-range MOS product, issued twice a day in twelve-hourly steps out to about 192 hours. Coarse, but the only station-calibrated numeric guidance that reaches the far end of a long weekend. This card shows it only as a labelled rough outlook and never as a resolved forecast. A station-calibrated MEX MOS product was read for this airport this run (state: ok).GFAGFA and prog charts — the Graphical Forecast for Aviation and the Weather Prediction Center surface progs, issued by the National Weather Service through the day; the surface prog series reaches 144 hours. They are raster images a pilot reads for fronts, pressure systems and precipitation shields. This page displays them with their issuing office and valid time and never interprets them: no category, wind, ceiling, ranking or go/no-go here is derived from an image. A published WPC surface chart matches this period and is shown in the dropdown with its issuing office and valid time. 4 · Planning gates

Everything the page does

  • Per-source state, validity horizon, and target-date coverage for every destination
  • Explicit unavailable/out-of-horizon target cells; no static weather fallback
  • Per-airport expandable detail — current observations, covered forecasts, dep/dest METAR temperatures
  • Four-day KLZU change-window board with four outbound/return planning alternatives
  • Source-labelled TAF/MOS flight-category guidance only when a source interval actually covers the planned window — a day with no covering interval shows an explicit unavailable/out-of-horizon state instead of a category, never an implied one
  • Timed NWS weather, wind-favored runway (magnetic, from each airport's own runways), gust, and material crosswind context wherever the forecast supplies them
  • Raw METAR/TAF + data-sources dropdown per airport
  • FAA Airport Status & Delays with known, unsupported, and unavailable states
  • Best-effort 100LL fuel prices
  • Auto-refreshed about 4x a day by an hourly scheduler that republishes once 6 h have passed since the last publish, so refresh times drift; the last-updated stamp is exact and the next-run stamp is an estimate
  • Quick links (Flight Circle, ForeFlight, FlightAware) + Feedback
  • FAA chart-cycle stamp (current VFR Sectional + Chart Supplement)
  • Download PDF — print-ready, color-preserving (semantic colors kept on paper)
  • Deterministic evidence-backed page; external AI aviation prose is withheld pending a validated evidence schema, so the executive-summary region shows an explicit pending-feature placeholder instead of generated text
  • Model-labeled MOS target-window outlook per airport (Iowa State GFS with conditional GFS Extended/MEX), with runtime and validity horizon shown
  • Expandable NWS FFC pattern summary and extended outlook inside the KLZU board
  • Per-airport chart links: SkyVector & AirNav/Chart Supplement (deep links)
  • FAA NMS owner-approved production source NOTAM adapter with explicit per-airport source states; active on this page as the owner-approved production source, and never a substitute for an official briefing
  • Full run archive: run_manifest.json with all data + provenance log
